questions.question: A current of 5 A flows through a straight wire of length 2 m placed in a uniform magnetic field of 0.4 T. If the wire makes an angle of 60° with the field, the force experienced by the wire is:
questions.explanation:
Force on a current-carrying conductor:
F = BIL sin θ
Given:
•
•
•
•

B = 0.4 T
I=5A
L=2m
θ = 60°

Substituting:
F = (0.4)(5)(2)(sin 60°)
F = 4 × 0.866
F ≈ 3.46 N
Answer: C

questions.question: The magnetic flux through a loop of area 0.5 m² is maximum when the plane of the loop is:
questions.explanation:
Magnetic flux is:
Φ = BA cos θ
Flux becomes maximum when θ = 0°.
This means the area vector is parallel to the magnetic field, so the plane of the loop is
perpendicular to the field.
Answer: C

questions.question: If a charged particle moves in a circle of radius R in a magnetic field B, then the momentum of the particle is:
questions.explanation:
For circular motion in a magnetic field:
mv²/R = qvB
Simplifying:
mv = qBR
Since momentum p = mv:
p = qBR
Answer: A

questions.question: In a velocity selector, the electric field E and magnetic field B are adjusted such that a particle of charge q and mass m passes undeflected. The velocity of the particle is:
questions.explanation:
In a velocity selector:
qE = qvB
Cancelling q:
v = E/B


This velocity does not depend on mass or charge.
Answer: B

questions.question: Two parallel wires carry currents I1 and I2 in the same direction. The force per unit length between them is:
questions.explanation:
Two parallel wires carrying current in the same direction attract each other.
Answer: C

questions.question: The magnetic field at the center of a circular coil of N turns and radius r carrying current I is given by:
questions.explanation:
Magnetic field at the center of a circular coil:
B = μ₀NI/2r
Answer: A

questions.question: The SI unit of magnetic flux is:
questions.explanation:
The SI unit of magnetic flux is Weber (Wb).
1 Wb = 1 T·m²
Answer: B

questions.question: A solenoid of length L has N turns. If the length of the solenoid is doubled while the number of turns remains the same, the magnetic field inside the solenoid:
questions.explanation:
Field inside a solenoid:
B = μ₀nI
Where:
n = N/L
If length doubles, n becomes half.


Therefore magnetic field also becomes half.
Answer: C

questions.question: Lenz’s Law is a consequence of the law of conservation of:
questions.explanation:
Lenz’s Law follows the law of conservation of energy because induced current always opposes
the change producing it.
Answer: D

questions.question: An electron moves with velocity v in a magnetic field B. The force on the electron is zero if:

options.D: The electron is moving in a circle

questions.explanation:
Magnetic force:
F = qvB sin θ
If velocity is parallel to magnetic field:
θ = 0°
sin 0° = 0
Therefore force becomes zero.
Answer: B

questions.question: The radius of the path of a charged particle in a magnetic field is inversely proportional to:
questions.explanation:
Radius of path:
r = mv/qB
Thus:
r ∝ 1/B
Radius is inversely proportional to magnetic field strength.


Answer: C

questions.question: A rectangular loop of area A is placed in a magnetic field B. If the plane of the loop makes an angle θ with the field, the magnetic flux is:
questions.explanation:
If θ is angle between plane and field:
Φ = BA cos(90° − θ)
Therefore:
Φ = BA sin θ
Answer: B

questions.question: The magnetic field produced by a long straight wire carrying current I at a distance r is:
questions.explanation:
Magnetic field due to long straight wire:
B = μ₀I/2πr
Answer: B

questions.question: In a seismometer, the induced e.m.f. is directly proportional to the:
questions.explanation:
In a seismometer, induced e.m.f. depends on relative motion between magnet and coil.
Therefore it depends on relative displacement.
Answer: C

questions.question: When a ferrous core is inserted into a solenoid, the magnetic field:
questions.explanation:
Ferrous cores increase magnetic permeability.
Hence magnetic field inside solenoid increases.
Answer: C

questions.question: The path of a charged particle entering a magnetic field at an angle of 0 < θ < 90° is:
questions.explanation:
Velocity component perpendicular to field causes circular motion.
Parallel component causes linear motion.
Combined motion becomes helical.
Answer: C

questions.question: The torque on a current-carrying coil of N turns and area A in a magnetic field B is maximum when the plane of the coil is:
questions.explanation:
Torque on current loop:
τ = NIAB cos α
Torque is maximum when α = 0°.
Thus plane of coil is parallel to magnetic field.
Answer: B

questions.question: A charge q moving with velocity v enters a region where both E and B exist. The total force is:
questions.explanation:
Total electromagnetic force:
F = qE + q(v × B)
This is Lorentz force.
Answer: B

questions.question: The dot product of magnetic flux density and the area vector is:
questions.explanation:
Magnetic flux is the dot product of magnetic field and area vector.
Φ=B·A


Answer: B

questions.question: Two protons are moving parallel to each other with the same velocity. The net force between them is the sum of:
questions.explanation:
Moving protons experience:
•
•

Electric repulsion
Magnetic interaction

Thus total force is sum of electric and magnetic forces.
Answer: B

questions.question: A magnetic field line shows the direction in which a _____ would point.
questions.explanation:
Magnetic field direction is the direction in which the north pole of a compass points.
Answer: C

questions.question: The sensitivity of a galvanometer is increased by:

options.C: Decreasing the area of the coil

questions.explanation:
Sensitivity of galvanometer increases with number of turns.
Answer: B

questions.question: A current-carrying conductor is placed in a magnetic field. It experiences no force if it is:
questions.explanation:
Force:
F = BIL sin θ
If conductor is parallel to field:
θ = 0°
Force becomes zero.


Answer: A

questions.question: The energy stored in the magnetic field of an inductor is:
questions.explanation:
Energy stored in inductor:
U = 1/2 LI²
Answer: A

questions.question: If the speed of a charged particle in a magnetic field is doubled, the radius of its circular path:
questions.explanation:
Radius:
r = mv/qB
Thus:
r∝v
Doubling speed doubles radius.
Answer: C

questions.question: The work done by a magnetic force on a moving charge is:
questions.explanation:
Magnetic force is perpendicular to motion.
Therefore work done is zero.
Answer: C

questions.question: A galvanometer is converted into an ammeter by connecting:
questions.explanation:
Ammeter requires low resistance.
So a low resistance shunt is connected in parallel.


Answer: A

questions.question: The unit of magnetic flux density is Tesla, which is also:
questions.explanation:
Using:
B = F/IL
Units become:
N/(A·m)
Answer: B

questions.question: Faraday’s law states that the induced e.m.f. is equal to the:

options.A: Rate of change of magnetic flux

questions.explanation:
Faraday’s Law:
ε = −N(dΦ/dt)
Induced e.m.f. equals rate of change of magnetic flux.
Answer: A

questions.question: A cyclotron is used to accelerate:
questions.explanation:
Cyclotrons accelerate heavy charged particles like protons and alpha particles. Electrons become
relativistic too quickly.
Answer: C

questions.question: The direction of the magnetic field produced by a current-carrying solenoid depends on:
questions.explanation:
The direction of magnetic field in a solenoid depends on the direction of current according to the
Right-Hand Grip Rule.
Answer: B

questions.question: If the magnetic flux linked with a coil changes by 2 × 10^-2 Wb in 0.01 s, the induced e.m.f. is:
questions.explanation:
Using:
ε = ΔΦ/Δt
ε = (2 × 10^-2)/(0.01) = 2 V
Answer: A

questions.question: A charged particle is projected into a magnetic field. Its kinetic energy:
questions.explanation:
Magnetic force changes only direction, not speed. Therefore kinetic energy remains constant.
Answer: C

questions.question: The force between two parallel wires carrying current in opposite directions is:
questions.explanation:
Parallel wires carrying current in opposite directions repel each other.
Answer: B

questions.question: The magnetic field inside a long solenoid is:
questions.explanation:
The magnetic field inside a long solenoid is uniform because field lines are parallel and equally
spaced.
Answer: C

questions.question: The e/m ratio of an electron is approximately:
A transformer works on the principle of:
questions.explanation:
A transformer works on the principle of mutual induction.
Answer: B

questions.question: The magnetic flux through a surface of area A held parallel to a uniform magnetic field B is:
questions.explanation:
If the surface is parallel to the field:
θ = 90°
Φ = BA cos 90° = 0
Answer: C

questions.question: Fleming’s Left-Hand Rule is used to find the direction of:
questions.explanation:
Fleming’s Left-Hand Rule gives the direction of magnetic force on a conductor.
Answer: B

questions.question: The magnetic field at a point P at distance r from a current element Idl is given by:
questions.explanation:
Biot-Savart Law gives the magnetic field due to a current element.
Answer: B

questions.question: In a galvanometer, the scale is linear because of:
questions.explanation:
A radial magnetic field makes galvanometer scale linear.


Answer: B

questions.question: An alpha particle and a proton enter a magnetic field with the same velocity. The ratio of radii of their paths (rα/rp) is:
questions.explanation:
For alpha particle:
r = mv/qB
rα/rp = (4u/2e)/(u/e) = 2
Answer: B

questions.question: The unit of mutual inductance is:
questions.explanation:
SI unit of mutual inductance is Henry.
Answer: A

questions.question: A square loop of side L carries current I. The magnetic field at its center is:
questions.explanation:
Magnetic field at center of loop is inversely proportional to side length.
B ∝ 1/L
Answer: B

questions.question: The velocity of a particle that passes undeflected through a velocity selector is independent of its:
questions.explanation:
Velocity selector formula:
v = E/B
It does not depend on mass or charge.
Answer: C

questions.question: If the current in a solenoid is reversed, the magnetic poles:
questions.explanation:
Reversing current reverses magnetic poles.
Answer: B

questions.question: The force on a current-carrying wire in a magnetic field is called:
questions.explanation:
Force on a current-carrying conductor is called catapult force.
Answer: A

questions.question: Magnetic monopoles:
questions.explanation:
Magnetic monopoles do not exist naturally.
Answer: B

questions.question: The strength of the magnetic field of a solenoid can be increased by:
questions.explanation:
Magnetic field increases by:
•
•
•

Increasing turns
Increasing current
Using iron core

Answer: D

questions.question: A current I flows in a circular arc of radius R subtending angle θ at the center. The magnetic field at the center is:
questions.explanation:
Field due to circular arc:
B = μ₀Iθ/4πR


Answer: A

questions.question: The magnetic field lines inside a bar magnet run from:
questions.explanation:
Inside a bar magnet, magnetic field lines move from South to North.
Answer: B

questions.question: The force F on a charge q moving with velocity v in magnetic field B is always _____ to v.
questions.explanation:
Magnetic force is perpendicular to velocity because:
F = q(v × B)
Answer: B

questions.question: A galvanometer is converted into a voltmeter by connecting:
questions.explanation:
A voltmeter is made by connecting high resistance in series.
Answer: A

questions.question: The magnetic flux linkage is defined as:
questions.explanation:
Magnetic flux linkage:
= NΦ
Answer: B

questions.question: When the plane of a coil is perpendicular to a magnetic field, the flux is:
questions.explanation:
When plane is perpendicular to field, flux becomes maximum.


Answer: A

questions.question: The self-inductance of a solenoid is proportional to:
questions.explanation:
Self inductance:
L ∝ N²
Answer: B

questions.question: A metal rod of length L moves with velocity v perpendicular to a magnetic field B. The induced e.m.f. is:
questions.explanation:
Motional e.m.f.:
ε = vBL
Answer: A

questions.question: The direction of induced current is such that it opposes the cause. This is:
questions.explanation:
Lenz’s Law states induced current opposes the cause producing it.
Answer: B

questions.question: The SI unit of magnetic induction is:
questions.explanation:
SI unit of magnetic induction is Tesla.
Answer: B

questions.question: The magnetic field at a point on the axis of a solenoid is:
questions.explanation:
The magnetic field on the axis of a solenoid is directed along the axis.
Answer: A

questions.question: Two parallel wires carry 10 A each in the same direction. If the distance between them is doubled, the force between them:
questions.explanation:
Force between parallel wires:
F ∝ 1/r
If distance doubles, force becomes half.
Answer: B

questions.question: The core of a transformer is laminated to reduce:
questions.explanation:
Transformer cores are laminated to reduce eddy current losses.
Answer: B

questions.question: The magnetic flux density B is a:
questions.explanation:
Magnetic flux density has magnitude and direction, so it is a vector quantity.
Answer: B

questions.question: A charge q is at rest in a very strong magnetic field. The force on it is:
questions.explanation:
Magnetic force:
F = qvB sin θ
If the charge is at rest, v = 0, therefore force is zero.
Answer: C

questions.question: The time period of a charged particle in a magnetic field is independent of its:
questions.explanation:
Time period in magnetic field:
T = 2πm/qB
Velocity cancels out, so time period is independent of velocity.
Answer: C

questions.question: The sensitivity of a voltmeter is given by:
questions.explanation:
Sensitivity of voltmeter:
S = 1/Ifsd
Answer: B

questions.question: If a charged particle enters a magnetic field at 90°, its path is:
questions.explanation:
When a charged particle enters perpendicular to magnetic field, it moves in a circular path.
Answer: B

questions.question: The value of μ0 is:
questions.explanation:
Permeability of free space:
μ₀ = 4π × 10^-7 T·m/A
Answer: A

questions.question: An electron and a proton enter a magnetic field with the same kinetic energy. The radius of the path of:
questions.explanation:
Radius:


r = √(2mK)/qB
For same kinetic energy, radius is proportional to √m.
Since proton is heavier, its radius is larger.
Answer: B

questions.question: The torque on a current loop is zero when the angle between B and the area vector is:
questions.explanation:
Torque:
τ = mB sin θ
If θ = 0°, torque becomes zero.
Answer: A

questions.question: A long solenoid has n turns per unit length. The field at its end is:
questions.explanation:
Magnetic field at end of solenoid:
= 1/2 μ₀nI
Answer: B

questions.question: The e/m ratio for a particle is X. If its velocity is doubled, its e/m ratio becomes:
questions.explanation:
e/m ratio is a property of particle and does not depend on velocity.
Answer: C

questions.question: A galvanometer of resistance G is shunted by resistance S. The effective resistance is:
questions.explanation:
Effective resistance of galvanometer and shunt:


Req = GS/(G + S)
Answer: B

questions.question: Which of the following is not a unit of magnetic induction?
questions.explanation:
N·m/A is not a unit of magnetic induction.
Answer: D

questions.question: Magnetic flux density is also known as:
questions.explanation:
Magnetic flux density is also called magnetic induction.
Answer: B

questions.question: The radius of the path of a particle of mass m and charge q moving with velocity v in field B is r. If B is tripled, r becomes:
questions.explanation:
Radius:
r ∝ 1/B
If magnetic field triples, radius becomes one-third.
Answer: B

questions.question: The current in a wire points North. If it is in a magnetic field pointing East, the force is:
questions.explanation:
Using Right-Hand Rule:
Current → North
Field → East
Force acts downward.
Answer: B

questions.question: A solenoid of 1000 turns per meter carries 2 A. The field inside is:
questions.explanation:
Using:
B = μ₀nI
B = (4π × 10^-7)(1000)(2)
B = 8π × 10^-4 T
Answer: D

questions.question: The work done by an external agent to move a charge q in a magnetic field B with velocity v is zero because:
questions.explanation:
Magnetic force is perpendicular to velocity, so no work is done.
Answer: B

questions.question: The unit of L/R (inductance/resistance) is:
questions.explanation:
Time constant of RL circuit:
τ = L/R
Unit is seconds.
Answer: A

questions.question: Two parallel wires carry current in same direction. If one current is doubled, the force:
questions.explanation:
Force between wires:
F ∝ I₁I₂
Doubling one current doubles force.


Answer: A

questions.question: A galvanometer shows full scale deflection for 10 mA. To measure 100 A, the shunt should be:
questions.explanation:
To measure large current, shunt resistance must be very low.
Answer: B

questions.question: The force on a charge q in B is F. If the charge is −q, the force is:
questions.explanation:
Changing q to −q reverses direction of force.
Answer: B

questions.question: The magnetic field due to a circular loop at a very large distance x from its center follows:
questions.explanation:
At large distance, magnetic field of loop behaves like dipole field:
B ∝ 1/x³
Answer: C

questions.question: An ideal ammeter has:
questions.explanation:
Ideal ammeter has zero resistance.
Answer: A

questions.question: An ideal voltmeter has:
questions.explanation:
Ideal voltmeter has infinite resistance.
Answer: B

questions.question: The magnetic field at the center of a solenoid of length L and turns N is B. At the ends, it is:
questions.explanation:
Field at end of solenoid is half the field at center.
Answer: B

questions.question: A proton enters a magnetic field from the left. If it deflects upwards, the field direction is:
questions.explanation:
Using Right-Hand Rule, magnetic field must be into the page.
Answer: A

questions.question: The ratio of magnetic flux to area is:
questions.explanation:
Magnetic flux density:
B = Φ/A
Answer: A

questions.question: The force per unit length between two wires 1 m apart carrying 1 A each is:
questions.explanation:
Force per unit length between two wires:
F/L = μ₀I₁I₂/2πr
Substituting:
•
•

I₁ = I₂ = 1 A
r=1m

F/L = 2 × 10^-7 N/m
Answer: A

questions.question: The magnetic flux through a coil of N turns is Φ. The total flux linkage is:
questions.explanation:
Total magnetic flux linkage:
= NΦ
Answer: B

questions.question: A charged particle is moving in a magnetic field. Its velocity vector:
questions.explanation:
Magnetic force changes only the direction of velocity, not its magnitude.
Answer: B

questions.question: If the number of turns in a coil is doubled, the induced e.m.f.:
questions.explanation:
Induced e.m.f.:
ε∝N
Doubling turns doubles induced e.m.f.
Answer: B

questions.question: The SI unit of μ0I/(2πr) is:
questions.explanation:
μ₀I/2πr gives magnetic field, whose SI unit is Tesla.
Answer: A

questions.question: The magnetic field of a bar magnet is strongest at the:
questions.explanation:
Magnetic field of a bar magnet is strongest at the poles.
Answer: B

questions.question: A current-carrying wire is placed along the axis of a solenoid. The force on the wire is:
questions.explanation:
Inside a solenoid, magnetic field is parallel to its axis.
If wire is along the axis, θ = 0° and force becomes zero.
Answer: B

questions.question: The cyclotron frequency does not depend on the:
questions.explanation:
Cyclotron frequency:
f = qB/2πm
It does not depend on radius.
Answer: C

questions.question: The force F = q(v × B) is also called:
questions.explanation:
F = q(v × B) is called Lorentz force.
Answer: B

questions.question: If B is uniform, the line integral of B around a closed path is:
questions.explanation:
The line integral of magnetic field around a closed path equals μ₀ times current enclosed.
This is Ampere’s Circuital Law.
Answer: B
